Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit; leaves may yellow, curl, and drop early, and fruit can crack.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Remove and destroy fallen leaves and infected fruit. Apply a fungicide per local label during wet spring weather; ask an extension service about timing.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant scab-resistant varieties and prune to improve airflow and drying.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Dark sunken rot on fruit, often starting at the blossom end, with concentric rings of tiny black dots; leaves may brown and blight.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune out infected branches and remove mummified fruit, disinfecting tools between cuts. Use a labeled fungicide only if local advice recommends it.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Clean up overwintering fruit and cankers, and choose resistant varieties where available.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Orange-yellow spots with red borders on leaves and horn-like orange growths underneath; fruit may show yellow spots and distortion.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Remove nearby juniper or cedar hosts if practical and prune infected twigs. Apply a labeled fungicide at bud break as advised locally.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Plant resistant apple varieties and avoid planting close to juniper or cedar.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green, intact, and free of spots, mold, or distortion, and fruit develops normally.
Apple___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal watering, feeding, and pruning.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Prune annually for airflow and clear fallen leaves to keep the tree healthy.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Foliage is uniformly green with no spotting, curling, or mold, and berries develop normally.
Blueberry___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; maintain normal watering and feeding.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Keep soil acidic and well-drained, and water at the base to avoid wet foliage.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White to gray powdery coating on leaves, shoots, and fruit; leaves may curl and distort.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Prune out heavily infected shoots and improve airflow. Apply a labeled fungicide per local guidance if needed.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties and avoid overhead watering to keep foliage dry.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are clean green with no powdery growth, spots, or curling, and fruit looks normal.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal care.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Prune for airflow and monitor trees weekly during the growing season.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.display_name: Corn (maize) — Cercospora leaf spot Gray leaf spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long narrow gray-brown lesions between leaf veins that can merge and kill whole leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Rotate out of corn and destroy crop residue after harvest. Use a labeled fungicide only if local advisors recommend it.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, rotate crops, and manage residue to reduce spores.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small reddish-brown pustules on leaves that rupture to a powdery rust color, usually in warm humid weather.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: In small plantings, remove badly affected leaves; field fungicide is rarely needed. Follow local advice.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Grow resistant hybrids and plant early to avoid peak rust pressure.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long gray-green to tan lesions running along leaves that can merge and blight foliage.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Rotate crops and bury or remove residue after harvest. Apply a labeled fungicide where local conditions warrant it.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Use resistant hybrids and rotate corn with non-host crops.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green and upright without lesions, rust, or blighting, and ears develop normally.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal care.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops and plant resistant hybrids to keep plants vigorous.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with dark borders and tiny black dots, plus dark shriveled rotting fruit.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and fruit and clean up fallen debris. Apply a labeled fungicide per local extension advice.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Prune for airflow, destroy overwintering debris, and plant resistant varieties.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Yellowing leaves with dark speckling and tiger-stripe patterns, and black spots or internal discoloration in berries.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: There is no cure; remove and destroy badly affected vines. Prune out infected wood and sterilize tools between vines.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Avoid wounding vines, prune in dry weather, and use clean tools.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Angular brown to dark leaf spots, often with a pale halo, that can merge and cause leaf drop.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Remove infected leaves and improve canopy airflow. Apply a labeled fungicide if local advisors recommend it.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Prune canopies for air movement and avoid overhead irrigation.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green and free of spots, yellowing, or mold, and clusters develop normally.
Grape___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal care.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Prune for airflow and monitor vines regularly through the season.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Yellow mottled leaves with uneven blotching, small misshapen fruit, and twig dieback.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: There is no cure; remove infected trees to limit spread and contact local authorities about testing.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Plant certified disease-free stock and control the psyllid vector per local guidance.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit that turn dark and may pit or crack, sometimes with yellow halos.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and fruit where practical. Apply a labeled bactericide per local extension advice.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use resistant varieties and avoid overhead watering to keep foliage dry.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green and unspotted with normal fruit set and no cracking or pitting.
Peach___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal care.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Prune for airflow and monitor weekly for early signs of disease.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit that become raised and scabby and may crack.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove infected plants and avoid handling wet foliage. Apply a labeled bactericide per local extension advice.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed, rotate crops, and avoid overhead irrigation.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green and turgid with no spots or lesions, and peppers form normally.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal care.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Water at the soil level and rotate crops each season.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves, with yellowing and leaf death as lesions spread.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected leaves and destroy plant debris after harvest. Apply a labeled fungicide per local advice.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, use certified seed, and water at the base to keep foliage dry.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked dark patches on leaves and stems with a white mold rim in humid weather, and brown rot on tubers.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants promptly and avoid handling wet foliage. Apply a labeled fungicide per local extension guidance.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed, avoid overhead watering, and destroy cull piles.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Foliage is green and vigorous without lesions or mold, and tubers develop normally.
Potato___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal care.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Use certified seed, rotate crops, and hill soil to protect tubers.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Canes and leaves look green and healthy with no spots, wilting, or mold, and fruit sets normally.
Raspberry___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal care.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune out spent canes and space plants for good airflow.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green and free of lesions or yellowing, and pods fill normally.
Soybean___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal care.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops and use disease-free seed to maintain plant health.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves and stems that spread and can cause yellowing and leaf drop.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Remove heavily infected leaves and improve airflow. Apply a labeled fungicide per local advice if needed.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties, space plants well, and water at the base.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small purple-red spots that enlarge into dry brown patches with purple borders, usually on older leaves.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Remove affected leaves and destroy debris after harvest. Apply a labeled fungicide if local advisors recommend it.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Use resistant varieties, rotate plantings, and avoid overhead watering.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green and unspotted with no browning, and fruit develops normally.
Strawberry___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal care.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Remove old foliage and keep beds well-drained and weed-free.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit that become scabby and may crack, sometimes with yellow halos.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and fruit and avoid working with wet plants. Apply a labeled bactericide per local extension advice.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed, rotate crops, and avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on lower leaves, which yellow and drop as the disease moves upward.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected leaves and destroy debris. Apply a labeled fungicide per local guidance when spots appear.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, stake plants for airflow, and water at the soil level.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked patches on leaves and stems with white mold in humid weather, and firm brown rot on fruit.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately and avoid wet foliage. Apply a labeled fungicide per local extension advice.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties, avoid overhead watering, and destroy volunteer plants and culls.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Yellow spots on upper leaves with olive-green velvety mold underneath, often in humid greenhouses.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Remove infected leaves and improve ventilation and airflow. Apply a labeled fungicide per local advice.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Reduce humidity, space plants, and avoid wetting foliage.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small round gray-brown spots with dark borders and tiny black dots, causing leaves to yellow and drop.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove spotted leaves and destroy debris after harvest. Apply a labeled fungicide per local advice if needed.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Rotate crops for at least two years and avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.display_name: Tomato — Spider mites Two-spotted spider mite
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling on leaves with tiny webbing; leaves may turn bronze and dry out.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Wash mites off with a strong water spray or apply a labeled miticide per local advice. Remove badly infested leaves.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Keep plants well-watered and avoid dusty hot dry conditions that favor mites.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Dark circular spots with concentric rings on leaves, stems, and fruit that can merge and cause leaf drop.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and improve airflow. Apply a labeled fungicide per local extension guidance.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Rotate crops, avoid overhead watering, and plant resistant varieties where available.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.display_name: Tomato — Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upward, become small and yellow, and plants are stunted with poor fruit set.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: There is no cure; remove infected plants to limit spread and control whiteflies per local advice.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Plant resistant varieties and use whitefly nets or labeled controls to limit the vector.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green leaves with puckering and distortion, plus stunted misshapen fruit.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: There is no cure; remove and destroy infected plants and disinfect tools and hands.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use certified seed, control aphids, and avoid handling plants when wet.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are green, expanded, and free of spots, curling, or mold, and fruit develops normally.
Tomato___healthy.treatment: No treatment is needed; continue normal watering, feeding, and pruning.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops and monitor plants weekly for early pest or disease signs.
